title: What happens when a hurricane reaches the coast?

lines.text: When a Category 5 hurricane slams into the coast, what actually causes the most catastrophic damage?
lines.caps: What causes the most *damage | when a *hurricane hits?

lines.text: Most people fear the one hundred and fifty mile per hour winds, but wind isn't the primary killer.
lines.caps: Winds are scary, but *water | is the real *killer

lines.text: The storm's central low pressure and violent winds act like a giant bulldozer pushing the ocean forward.
lines.caps: Winds act like a *bulldozer | pushing the *ocean

lines.text: This creates a massive wall of seawater called a storm surge, rising over twenty feet above sea level.
lines.caps: Creates a *twenty-foot wall | of crushing storm *surge!

lines.text: A single cubic yard of water weighs nearly one ton, easily demolishing brick homes and concrete bridges.
lines.caps: One cubic yard of *water | weighs a full *ton

lines.text: Once over land, the hurricane loses warm ocean fuel, weakening into torrential inland rain deluges.
Storm surge causes nearly ninety percent of all direct hurricane fatalities.
lines.caps: Storm surge causes *90% | of all hurricane *deaths!
